AI providers

Use my relay as the AI server
Speech and text go to your relay, which calls the AI provider with the key stored on it. The provider key then stays on the relay and is not needed here. Fill in the relay address and token under Privacy (Sync voice notes with my relay)
Stored on this phone, not encrypted. A server of your own may need no key. Plain http works only for this phone, your local network and Tailscale.

Voice & audio

Language
Auto can switch on short phrases
Microphone
Which microphone Vox listens to. The phone's own microphone unless you pick one. If dictation says it heard nothing, try another.
AI cleanup
Removes fillers, fixes punctuation, applies corrections
Skip AI cleanup for phrases shorter than N words
Short phrases skip the AI, which is faster: Vox only drops um and uh, writes spoken punctuation and fixes capitals. 1 cleans up everything (1 to 20)
Cleanup strength
Light keeps every word you said and only fixes punctuation, capitals, spelling and paragraphs. Standard also removes fillers and false starts. If the cleanup lost words, Vox types them as spoken
Lists and paragraphs
Auto and Lists only turn a list you say (first, second; point one, point two; bullet point; pehla, doosra) into a list. Off keeps the text flat. Saying commas never makes a list

Privacy

What leaves this phone: your audio and its transcript go to your voice server, and the cleanup text goes to your cleanup server (both through your relay when it is the AI server). Your dictionary goes with them as spelling hints, including the words Learn from my corrections adds. Voice notes are kept in this phone's note store and send no app name; with sync on, their text also goes to your relay. Vox has no analytics and no server of its own.

Keep dictation history
Saves what you dictate on this phone, not encrypted. Off saves nothing
Learn from my corrections
Sync voice notes with my relay
Keeps your voice notes the same on your phone and PCs through a relay you run yourself (a small server, for example on a Raspberry Pi, reached over Tailscale). While on, the relay receives the full text, raw transcript, tags and device name of each voice note, and your About you text, dictionary, people, snippets, learned cleanup rules, default style, cleanup switch and language. Needs its address and token
Stored on this phone, not encrypted. Plain http works only for this phone, your local network and Tailscale.
Sent to the relay and shown on its page and on the notes made here. Blank uses the phone model.
Also share my provider settings and API keys
Off by default. When on, the AI provider, models and API keys are copied to your other devices through the relay, so anyone with the relay token can read them. Turning this off here removes this device's keys from the relay once. Any other device that still shares keys will put them back, so turn it off on every device.
About you
Added to every cleanup request, so it goes to your cleanup server. While sync is on it is also copied to your relay. Edit it on the Dictionary tab

How to set up the relay

The relay is a small program that keeps your notes and settings in one place for your phone and PCs. Run it on something that is always on, such as a Raspberry Pi. Tailscale must be installed and signed in on it and on this device, with HTTPS turned on for your tailnet (Tailscale admin console, DNS page).

  1. On the Pi, put relay.py (from the relay folder of Vox) where the service will run it.
    sudo mkdir -p /opt/vox-relay
sudo cp relay.py /opt/vox-relay/
  2. Try it once by hand. It prints where it listens. Stop it with Ctrl+C.
    python3 /opt/vox-relay/relay.py --data-dir /tmp/vox-relay-test --show-token
  3. Install it as a service, so it starts at boot and restarts if it stops (vox-relay.service is next to relay.py).
    sudo cp vox-relay.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now vox-relay
  4. Read the token. Keep it private: anyone with the token and a way to reach the relay can read your notes.
    sudo cat /var/lib/vox-relay/relay.json
  5. Publish it to your tailnet. This is what adds HTTPS. Never use tailscale funnel, which puts it on the open internet. The second command shows the address.
    sudo tailscale serve --bg 8765
tailscale serve status
  6. Enter that address (like https://your-pi.your-tailnet.ts.net) and the token in the fields above, then press Test connection. It tells you whether the relay is reachable, whether the token works, and the name this device shows under.

No Raspberry Pi? A Windows PC can run it: in the Vox tray menu tick Run relay on this PC, then run tailscale serve --bg 8765 in a terminal. It only works while that PC is on and Vox is running.

Devices on my relay
Phones and PCs that have used your relay, newest first, as the relay itself recorded them. Needs the relay address and token above; the only thing sent from here is this phone's name

Bubble diagnostics
If the bubble keeps disappearing, this shows why. It stays on this phone; copy it only if you want to share it
Android may close Vox in the background, and then the bubble disappears. Choose Vox in the list and set it to Not optimised (the wording differs by phone: Unrestricted, Don't optimise or Allow).
Install help: warnings and Restricted setting

Vox is installed from a file, not from Google Play, and it types for you through an accessibility service. Android and Play Protect are careful about exactly that, so one or two warnings are normal. Nothing in the app can switch them off.

  1. "Restricted setting" or the Vox switch is greyed out (Android 13 and newer). Open Settings, Accessibility, Vox dictation bubble and tap the switch once so Android shows its message. Then:
    On that screen tap the three dots (top right), then Allow restricted settings, confirm with your PIN or fingerprint, and turn the switch on. The menu entry only appears after the first try.
  2. Play Protect says "App blocked" or "Unknown app" while installing. Tap More details, then Install anyway (or Scan app first). Play Protect does not know Vox, and apps that use accessibility and come from a browser or file manager are treated strictly. Your phone may offer no way past it; then use the next step.
  3. Install from a computer instead. Turn on USB debugging (Settings, Developer options), connect the phone and run, from the folder with the APK:
    adb install -r Vox.apk
    Optional, only if Allow restricted settings never shows up (it may do nothing on your phone):
    adb shell cmd appops set com.minhaj.vox ACCESS_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS allow

A sideloaded app cannot fully avoid these warnings. The ways that remove them are Google Play (closed testing) or an app store such as F-Droid. Update with the same kind of file every time: Android only updates an app signed with the same key.
